rule: No process-global mutable state in production code: statics with interior mutability, thread-local slots, environment or working-directory reads at the point of use, process-wide hooks and child processes that inherit the live environment. Pass state through configuration and context instead, read the process's arguments and environment once at the entry point, and spawn children with env_clear() plus an explicit environment. check_process_globals.py fails on anything unlisted and on entries that no longer match, so this list only shrinks. 'debt' entries are scheduled for removal (dev-docs/ProcessGlobalsPlan.md in the glade-wz workspace); 'permanent' entries are read once at a program's entry point or carry no shared state.
source: scripts/checks/check_process_globals.py is gwz-core's checker at commit 730e7119 (gwz-dev workspace), vendored byte for byte; its own tests live there.

entries.name: env::args
entries.reason: The program reads its arguments once, at its entry point, and passes them down.

entries.name: libc::signal
entries.reason: A C signal handler, installed for SIGINT and SIGTERM, tears the children down through the PID statics. A signal task (tokio::signal) that owns the child handles needs neither (ProcessGlobalsPlan Step 4.2).

entries.name: Command::new
entries.reason: Spawns the node and the composed suppliers with the live process environment (it sets GLADE_HOME and inherits the rest); spawn them with env_clear() plus an explicit environment (ProcessGlobalsPlan Step 3.3).

entries.name: GWZ_PID
entries.reason: The gwz supplier's PID for the signal handler; goes with it (ProcessGlobalsPlan Step 4.2).

entries.name: GYLD_PID
entries.reason: The gyld supplier's PID for the signal handler; goes with it (ProcessGlobalsPlan Step 4.2).

entries.name: NODE_PID
entries.reason: The node's PID for the signal handler; goes with it (ProcessGlobalsPlan Step 4.2).
